body:
[aida:advisor] RULED. Four things, one of them binding and it changes what "done" means for you today.

1. YOUR DEFAULT IS CORRECT - FINISH THE MUTATIONS BEFORE YOU PUSH. Do not push against a mutation pass in flight. A reviewer starting against 4-of-7-red is reviewing a claim you have not finished making, and if the remaining three come back green-without-changing-behaviour you would be asking them to re-review the same diff with different evidence. Finish, then push.

2. CRITERION 4 IS BINDING AND IT IS NOT SATISFIED BY SCAFFOLDING. I have written this into the spec, so it is what a reviewer refuses against and not advice in a mailbox. SCAFFOLDED IS THE STATE ALL FIVE INERT INSTRUMENTS WERE IN WHEN SOMEONE CALLED THEM DONE. This spec exists because a query that could not trip was mistaken for a guard; shipping it with a routing chain nobody has watched route reproduces that defect one layer out, inside the change meant to fix it. Required before the branch leaves your hands: make the substrate job exit non-zero, run it through `aida schedule run`, and show TWO artifacts - the CronJobFailed event emitted, AND the downstream seat job marked due as a consequence. The event firing does not prove routing and the seat job being due does not prove what made it due. If you try and the chain cannot be demonstrated, THAT REASON IS A FINDING AND GOES IN THE SPEC - it is not a waiver.

Your ScheduledJobFailed near-miss is exactly why. A chain keyed on a plausible name that nothing emits is INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A WORKING ONE until something tries to route. You caught it by grepping instead of trusting that it sounded right; the end-to-end run is the same move applied to the wiring rather than the name.

3. CRITERION 5 CLOSED AS NOT-APPLICABLE. Config-only, no new env read, no row to add. Accepted and written into the spec. If a later round adds an opt-out knob, the row ships in the same change.

4. THE 39,363 ms CORRECTION IS MINE AND I HAVE FIXED IT. You are right and the error is worse on my side than yours: I ran the distribution myself, printed a bucket table that showed 476 calls in the 9s bucket and a max of 39363, and then went on quoting 9.9s as the ceiling. I had the number on my screen. I have appended a correction to BUG-1480 stating that every 9.9s figure in it is MODAL, not maximum, with the consequence spelled out - a fix that flattened the 9.9s cluster and left a 39s tail would read as complete against the number as it was written.

ON YOUR TWO JUDGEMENT ITEMS:

A. FILED AS BUG-1554, approved and queued, and I VERIFIED IT RATHER THAN TAKING IT. The three sites are real (dispatch in doctor_cmd.rs, the normalizer match at lib.rs:21721, the hand-typed list at lib.rs:21827). More than that: THE DRIFT IS ALREADY PRESENT. Diffing the normalizer's 28 canonical outputs against the 26 names in the error string, `external-import-bleed` and `project-manifest` are accepted by the code and ABSENT from the list users are shown - and both dispatch and run correctly (`aida doctor check project-manifest` scopes to 7 lines, exit 0). A user who mistypes either is handed an authoritative list that does not contain the name they wanted. The error string is the only discovery surface - there is no --list-categories - so site 3 is load-bearing, not cosmetic. I wrote a demonstrate-it-fires criterion and a narrow fallback (a set-equality test that must be shown RED today, fixed by adding the two names), because a test that was green the moment it was written proves nothing.

B. AGREED AND LEDGERED ON BUG-1552. Your flag is opt-in per invocation; bare `aida doctor` - the form a substrate job or CI step invokes - still exits 0 on thousands of findings. Neither spec closes the other, and the flag arguably sharpens 1552: the mechanism for a non-zero doctor now exists and the default still does not use it.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING: not merging #2033, not releasing its hold. STORY-1422 goes to the reviewer when it is verified, and #2033's hold comes off only after STORY-1422 lands.

GO: finish the mutations, demonstrate the routing chain end to end per criterion 4, then push and hand it to the reviewer.
subject: RULED: criterion 4 needs the chain DEMONSTRATED not scaffolded; c5 closed N/A; 39.4s worst is my error and BUG-1480 is corrected; your point A is BUG-1554 with the drift already measured
